title: Are You an Objective Decision-Maker
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece explores what genuine objectivity looks like in leadership decision-making, acknowledging upfront that total objectivity is impossible since experience and bias inevitably shape judgment. The author instead frames objectivity as a discipline of creating distance: basing decisions on provable, testable evidence, consciously suppressing misleading intuition, and seeking diverse viewpoints to avoid echo chambers. Objective leaders are also described as more deliberate, pausing to reflect before deciding rather than rushing to judgment. The piece closes by tying perceived objectivity directly to how much trust colleagues place in a leader's decisions.
points: True objectivity is impossible, but the most trusted leaders work hard to reduce subjectivity anyway
Objective leaders base judgments on provable, testable evidence rather than personal feelings
They consciously suppress misleading intuition drawn from past experience when assessing new situations
Objective leaders pause to reflect and seek diverse viewpoints before reaching a decision
quotes: In comparison to other decision-makers, leaders viewed as objective are more trusted to reach the best possible decision.
Scholars contend that no one can be completely objective, as their beliefs and experience can’t be entirely ignored or disregarded.
They emphasize that the information used to reach a decision be provable, testable, or verifiable.
This focus on objectivity influences leaders to work hard at suppressing misleading intuition that springs from their experience.
Objectivity inspires confidence in both the decision and the decision-maker.
